source: Derek, 2026-10-07: "I want to add a variant to the tyranny chess ... Coriantmr chess after the book of mormon character. Last man standing is the king." Rules settled across two AskUserQuestion rounds, recorded as run-log decisions eb1e698d4d and cbd4125232 (the second states one reconciliation of mine for him to confirm: the line of succession still ends with pawns). Round 3 closed 2026-10-04 and is archived at _context/goal-tree-r3-closed.json. LESSON CARRIED FORWARD: round 3's contract checked the data and never the player's experience, so every release blocker here is an independent-implementation check or something done in the real page.

root.title: Tyranny Chess round 4: Coriantumr, a last-man-standing rule set beside Tyranny and standard
root.notes: Rules in one paragraph: king and queen slide up to 4 squares in any direction; every other piece moves as in chess; no check, checkmate, castling or self-capture; capturing a king is an ordinary capture; after any capture a side that still has pieces but no king and no queen has its closest bishop (else knight, rook, pawn) become a king; far-rank promotion also offers a king when the side has none; you win when the opponent has no pieces. Work happens on branch coriantumr; main and the live site are untouched until Derek says otherwise.
non_goals: Puzzles for Coriantumr. Puzzle mode stays Tyranny-only and is locked out of the variant.
An owner-picks pop-up for tied successors; Derek chose the fixed rule (queenside first) for now.
Any change to Tyranny or standard rules, results, puzzles or the existing tests' meaning.
Renaming the app, repository or live URL; the variant lives inside Tyranny Chess as a rules option.
Networked play, an opening book, or strength tuning beyond a sanity check.
Pushing or merging to main. That needs Derek's explicit yes.
must_not: Change any existing Tyranny or standard behavior: puzzles.json must regenerate byte for byte, perft values must not move, and no existing assertion may be removed or weakened.
Carry the variant only in page state: it rides on the board state and must survive every apply(), otherwise the engine silently reverts to standard rules mid-game and nothing fails.
Add a commander or ruler field to the board state. The derived rule (no king and no queen after a capture) is stateless on purpose.
Transform or retitle the queen when she takes command; Derek was explicit that she keeps her piece and title.
Call the engine correct because it agrees with itself. The independent reference must be written from the rules text in another language, and the hand-derived perft(3) = 9,122 must match.
State or imply that endgames are winnable, or are drawn, before the retrograde measurement exists.
Add a new banner comment before the GAME / UI banner in src/tyranny.html or put DOM code inside tests/extract.js's slices; both silently shrink or break the extracted engine.
Wait for a page timer with a fixed sleep, or pick a test fixture from the random deal or as 'the first match'. Round 3 found two flaky browser checks caused exactly that way.
Let the page's self-capture toggle reach Coriantumr rules: no self-capture, whatever the toggle says.
Ship any draw rule inside Coriantumr: the owner removed fifty-move, repetition and no-legal-move draws (his words: 'Remove them').
Treat the used-square lists as page state: they must live in the board state, or a position reached by undo or by the engine's search would forget them.
Read 'the royal piece has to sacrifice itself' as a pass: he said 'I guess you can build that the turn passes' only for the impossible case, and asked for the sacrifice.

Claim the last-piece rule or the showdown is solved or fair on the full board: the owner's reading was solved exactly only on 3x3 and 4x4 (and decided there by who moves first), the shared reading up to 5x5; say so.

Ban retreating or re-landing on a square in ordinary play to stop repetition: the owner said he does not want to discourage a retreat 'just for the sake of a rule'. The only repetition rule is the refused third occurrence.
Describe the last-piece rule as shared between the two pieces or as blocking slides: the owner chose side-specific lists with slides passing over used squares.

children.title: Movement, legality, succession, promotion and endings, in the engine

criteria.text: A king or queen slides up to 4 squares in each of 8 directions, blocked by the first piece on the ray, capturing an enemy there and never a friendly; every other piece moves exactly as in chess. Asserted on an empty board (27 moves from d4, 12 from a1, for both king and queen) and with blockers on each ray.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr.js 117 passed 0 failed 2026-10-07: queen and king on d4 empty board 27 moves; reach 3 and reach 5 mutants killed; tools/coriantumr-ref.py --check NO DRIFT (15 handmade + 300 sampled positions)

criteria.text: There is no check, checkmate or castling in a Coriantumr state: a move that leaves its own king capturable is legal, no castling move is ever generated, and capturing a king is an ordinary capture.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr.js: no castling move offered, never reports check, royal-safety filter mutant killed; reference agrees on every move of 300 sampled positions

criteria.text: There is no self-capture: for every position reached in the tests, legal(S, true) and legal(S, false) are identical in a Coriantumr state, so the page's self-capture setting cannot leak into the variant.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr.js: friendly pawn blocks the ray and cannot be captured; self-capture-leak mutant killed

criteria.text: Succession: after any capture that leaves a side with at least one piece but no king and no queen, exactly one piece of that side becomes a king: the closest bishop, else the closest knight, else rook, else pawn. Closest is the smallest squared straight-line distance to the capture square; ties go to the lower file, then the lower rank. Tested class by class, including ties on file and on rank.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr.js + golden fixture: crown order, squared distance (vs king-steps and city-block), file then rank ties; 8 succession mutants killed; independent Python reference matches in all cases

criteria.text: A queen alive when the king is captured is not changed in any way (same piece code, same square) and nothing else on that side changes; a queen captured while a king lives changes nothing either.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr.js: living queen stops the crowning, bishops stay bishops; mutant killed; browser R4-M4-AC3 shows the queen stays bq on h8

criteria.text: Over seeded random full games (fixed seeds, so the result cannot depend on a random deal), after every ply every non-empty side holds a king or a queen, and a side down to exactly one piece holds a king or a queen as that piece.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr.js: seeded random play 10 seeds, at least 5,000 plies, every non-empty side holds a king or queen, brokenInvariant 0

criteria.text: Far-rank promotion offers queen, rook, bishop and knight as in chess, and additionally KING exactly when the side has no king piece; a side that already has a king is never offered one.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr.js: no king piece offers Q R B N K; with a king no king is offered; two mutants killed; browser R4-M4-AC6 picker shows 5 then 4 buttons

criteria.text: A side with no pieces has lost: the side to move holding zero pieces scores as a loss and the game-over text names the winner as last man standing. No legal move with pieces left is a draw, and the 50-move and threefold-repetition draws apply. There is no insufficient-material draw unless R4-M2's measurement shows one is sound.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr-ai.js: capturing last piece scores as mate, no-piece side scores lost at the right ply; browser R4-M4-AC5 shows White wins last man standing

criteria.text: The variant rides on the board state and survives every apply(): across several seeds and at least 5,000 plies of seeded random play, every state reached from a Coriantumr start still has the variant set and still generates the 4-square king and queen reach at the end, while a standard or Tyranny state never gains the field.

children.title: Proof that the rules are right, and what endings can actually be won
Independent reference, hand-derived perft, retrograde endgame measurement

criteria.text: An independent implementation written from the rules text, in a different language (pure Python, not a transliteration of the JavaScript), agrees with the engine on perft depths 1 to 4 from at least four positions, including positions where a king is capturable and where a capture triggers succession within the horizon. The agreed numbers are committed as a golden fixture with the reference's provenance, and the reference has a --check mode.
criteria.evidence: tools/coriantumr-ref.py (pure Python, different board representation, global after-a-capture succession check) --check: NO DRIFT; tests/coriantumr-golden.json 15 handmade + 300 sampled with SHA-1 digests

criteria.text: From the start position perft(1), perft(2) and perft(3) equal 20, 400 and 9,122, the last derived by hand (8,902 plus 220: the king's extra reach after d3, d4, e4, f3 or f4 is +3, +3, +1, +2, +2 = 11, times 20 black replies) with the derivation written in the test, so the engine and the reference cannot share a misreading.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr.js perft(3) = 8902 + 20 x 11 = 9122 asserted; perft 1..4 = 20 / 400 / 9122 / 207622 equals Python reference

criteria.text: Endgame winnability is MEASURED, not assumed: a retrograde (backward) analysis over small material sets reports as plain counts which attacker sets can force the capture of a lone king and in how many moves, and the README states the result and what it does not cover.
criteria.evidence: tools/coriantumr-endgame.js --self-test 6000 positions 0 differ; counts in README table and _context/coriantumr-endgame.json; README states what it does not cover (pawns, 3+ attackers, 50-move and repetition)

criteria.text: The draw rules for the variant follow from that measurement and are recorded as a decision with the numbers. If annihilation cannot be forced in common endings, the shortfall is reported to Derek as a count before any extra rule is added; no rule is invented to hide it.
criteria.evidence: decision bc0293169a: no extra draw rule; shortfall reported to Derek as counts before any rule; draws stay no-legal-move, 50-move, repetition

criteria.text: In a Coriantumr state the search ignores king safety in both search and quiescence: in a constructed position where the only winning line leaves the engine's own king attacked, the engine plays it, and no check extension fires.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr-ai.js 27 passed 0 failed: a hanging king is captured by qsearch, no check extension (inCheck false with a king under attack); mutant that filters quiescence captures by king safety killed

criteria.text: Terminal scoring: the side to move with no pieces scores as lost at the right ply, so the engine finds the capture of the opponent's last piece and avoids a line that loses its own last piece.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr-ai.js: Rxe8 scored as mate, lone-king capture wins, no pieces scores lost at the right ply, no-move scores draw

criteria.text: Evaluation values king and queen as the same 4-square piece, has no king-safety or mop-up term, and is colour-symmetric: a position and its colour-flipped mirror score the same from each side's view.
criteria.evidence: tests/coriantumr-ai.js: king and queen same value, colour-symmetric evaluation over probed positions, asym 0; white-favoured mutant killed

criteria.text: Played games terminate and are reported as plain counts, not graded: 100 seeded engine-vs-random games and 20 engine-vs-engine games under a ply cap, with no illegal move and no exception; wins, draws, losses and mean length are recorded.

children.title: No draws, forced sacrifice, last pieces and refused repeats

criteria.text: No draws in Coriantumr: with the variant tag, outcome() reports neither the fifty-move rule nor threefold repetition nor a no-legal-move draw, and the engine search does not score a repeated position as a draw. Tyranny and standard keep every draw rule and their suites pass unchanged. Checked in the engine tests and in the real page on a position with the half-move clock past 100 and on a threefold-repeated position.
criteria.evidence: final tree 2026-10-07: tests/browser.js 297 passed 0 failed in five runs (three idle, two with 12 busy loops on 8 cores): a position with the half-move clock at 100 leaves overTxt null in Coriantumr, a shuffle stops one move short of a third occurrence (game not drawn) while the same clicks under Tyranny end 'Draw - threefold repetition' and a fifty-move position ends 'Draw - fifty-move rule' (controls); tests/coriantumr-ai.js 54 passed: a repeated position is not scored as a draw; page break 'fifty-move and repetition draws are back in the variant' killed (7 failing lines)

criteria.text: Sacrifice: when the side to move has no ordinary legal move and owns a royal piece, legal() returns exactly one move, the sacrifice of its king (else its queen on the lowest file, then the lowest rank). It removes that piece, applies the succession rule from the sacrificed square (a queen alive means nobody changes; none left means the closest bishop, knight, rook, pawn is crowned), and passes the turn. It is never offered when an ordinary move exists. Agreed by the independent Python reference's per-move digests and perft on constructed boxed-in positions, and by hand-derived cases.
criteria.evidence: final tree 2026-10-07: tests/coriantumr.js 239 passed: boxed-in king, queen-only royal, king plus queen, two queens (lowest file), two queens on one file (lowest rank), never offered while a move exists; Python reference digests and perft on the 22 handmade positions incl. those (python tools/coriantumr-ref.py --check: NO DRIFT); browser R4-M6-AC2: notice shown, two clicks sacrifice, closest pawn a7 crowned, message, Undo restores; 40 engine breaks killed incl. sacrifice never offered, wrong royal, wrong tie, piece left on board, succession skipped

criteria.text: Last pieces (the owner's side-specific ruling of 2026-10-07, replacing the shared-set showdown): when a side is down to exactly one piece, that piece may not land on a square it has stood on since it became the last piece (the square it stands on counts). Captures are exempt, a slide may pass over such a square, and the opponent's squares stay available. When both sides are down to one piece (the showdown) both lists start fresh at that moment. The lists ride on the board state through every apply(), appear nowhere else, and survive Undo. A last piece with no untouched landing square and no capture must sacrifice itself, which leaves its side with no pieces, so it loses. The Python reference agrees on every move digest and on perft(1..3) from constructed positions that carry lists.
criteria.evidence: final tree 2026-10-07: tests/coriantumr.js 239 passed, with these engine breaks each caught by 2 to 34 checks: lists never begin, a list never grows, every move grows both lists, the showdown does not start afresh, a FEN position has no first used square, a side with two pieces bound too, a capture onto a used square forbidden, used squares landed on again, the opponent's list binding the mover; python tools/coriantumr-ref.py --check: 'checked 22 handmade positions, 7 last-piece positions, 4 repetition positions and 300 sampled positions: NO DRIFT' (digests and perft(1..3) from constructed positions that carry lists); lists live only in S.lv (grep of src/tyranny.html), and tests/browser.js AC3 now undoes a move and a capture and shows the lists and shading come back with them (297 passed)
